annotation_description: Nethergoyf enters as a 0/1 with an empty graveyard, providing no immediate board presence. Against a mill opponent, Nihil Spellbomb would provide more strategic value as a proactive graveyard hate piece that could also cantrip later. Shadowspear is also arguable as it provides utility once a real creature arrives.

Casting Shadowspear on turn 2 instead of Nihil Spellbomb against a mill deck. The opponent is playing UB Mill (Flooded Strand, Island, Archive Trap/Glimpse the Unthinkable are typical). Nihil Spellbomb would provide graveyard exile capability which could be crucial against mill strategies and also protects against the opponent potentially using graveyard-based cards. Shadowspear's +1/+1, trample, and lifelink are nice on Nethergoyf, but the equip cost of 2 means it won't be equipped until turn 3 at earliest anyway. Meanwhile, Nihil Spellbomb could sit ready to exile the opponent's graveyard (less relevant) or more importantly be available as an artifact in the graveyard to boost Nethergoyf's power via card types. However, Shadowspear is also an artifact that could end up there. The real consideration is that against a mill deck, having Nihil Spellbomb ready to crack could be important, though it exiles the opponent's graveyard, not yours. Given Nethergoyf cares about YOUR graveyard card types, and the mill opponent will be filling YOUR graveyard, Nihil Spellbomb targeting yourself would be counterproductive. So actually Shadowspear is reasonable - it provides a clock with lifelink to race the mill plan. This is debatable but not clearly wrong.

The opponent has Thought-Knot Seer in hand, which is a 4/4 that will exile a card from GPT4om's hand when it enters. Nethergoyf is currently only a 2/3 (artifact and creature in graveyard after Nihil Spellbomb, but only 1 card type - artifact - so it's 1/2, or with Divest adding sorcery to GY it grows). Meanwhile, Thought-Knot Seer is a much more impactful card - it's a 4/4 body AND it exiles a nonland card from GPT4om's hand, which is devastating given the mill player's hand full of key spells like Fractured Sanity, Glimpse the Unthinkable, and Archive Traps. Nethergoyf can also escape from the graveyard later. Discarding TKS would protect the hand and remove a bigger threat.

Attacked with Hedron Crab (0/2) into a board with Nethergoyf (2/3). The Crab deals 0 damage so there's zero offensive value, but the opponent can freely block with Nethergoyf to kill the Crab, which is the mill deck's key engine piece for landfall triggers.

Declined to activate Urza's Saga to create a Construct token before declaring attackers. With only 3 mana available (Swamp, Urborg, Urza's Saga), they can't cast Thought-Knot Seer (4 mana) this turn anyway. Creating a Construct (which would be roughly 2/2 with Shadowspear + itself as artifacts) before combat would give an additional attacker alongside Nethergoyf.

The player discarded Polluted Delta instead of a less valuable card. With Hedron Crab on the battlefield, fetch lands are extremely powerful - each one triggers Hedron Crab to mill 3 cards. The player already has 3 Archive Traps in hand, and the opponent is about to search their library (Urza's Saga chapter III), which means all 3 Archive Traps can be cast for free. But future fetch lands provide additional mill triggers with Hedron Crab AND can trigger Archive Traps if drawn later. Meanwhile, Fractured Sanity costs UUU which is very difficult to cast with only 1 Island in play and no other blue sources, making it a reasonable discard candidate. Alternatively, one of the three Archive Traps could be discarded since having 3 is redundant when the opponent may not search again after this turn.

Discarding Flooded Strand to hand size is a mistake because Flooded Strand is a fetchland that serves a critical role in this mill deck. When played and cracked, it triggers Hedron Crab's landfall (milling 3 cards), enables searching the library (which lets opponents' Archive Traps be cast for free — but more importantly here, GPT4om is the one WITH Archive Traps), and provides color fixing. Meanwhile, the player has 3 Archive Traps in hand but only 1 Island on the battlefield and no way to cast Glimpse the Unthinkable or Fractured Sanity without more lands. Flooded Strand would help fix mana and trigger Hedron Crab. A better discard would be the third Archive Trap, since having 3 copies is redundant — they only work when the opponent searches their library, and the opponent (playing Eldrazi/artifacts) may not search often. Alternatively, one of the Fractured Sanity copies could be discarded since casting UUU is very difficult with current mana.

Playing Prismatic Vista before killing Hedron Crab with Fatal Push triggers landfall, milling 3 cards unnecessarily. If they crack Vista later, that's another 3 cards milled. Against a mill deck, this feeds the opponent's strategy.

With Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth on the battlefield, all lands already tap for black mana, making fetching a basic Swamp redundant. If Wastes is in the deck (very likely given Thought-Knot Seer and Kozilek's Command requiring colorless mana), fetching Wastes would provide both {B} (via Urborg) and {C}, enabling Thought-Knot Seer to be cast next turn with 4 lands.

Gem25P Vorthos has Thought-Knot Seer in hand which requires colorless mana ({3}{C}). They also have Kozilek's Command which requires {C}{C}. Fetching a Wastes would provide a colorless mana source, enabling casting Thought-Knot Seer next turn (with Wastes + 3 Swamps = {3}{C}). With Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth on the battlefield, the Wastes would also tap for black mana when needed, so there's virtually no downside to fetching Wastes over Swamp. By fetching Swamp instead, they have no way to produce colorless mana (Urza's Saga appears to have been sacrificed already), stranding Thought-Knot Seer and making Kozilek's Command harder to cast.

Failed to equip Shadowspear before combat. With 3 mana available (Swamp, Swamp, Urborg) and Shadowspear's equip cost of {2}, they could have equipped Nethergoyf to make it 5/6 with trample and lifelink, dealing 5 damage and gaining 5 life instead of just dealing 4. They'd still have 1 mana open for Fatal Push as interaction.

While equipping Shadowspear is reasonable, the player has exactly 3 mana available (2 for equip + 1 for Fatal Push) and could also kill Hedron Crab this turn. The reasoning focuses entirely on Shadowspear with no mention of also removing the opponent's key mill enabler. If they pass without also casting Fatal Push on Hedron Crab, that would be a clear miss.

Failed to kill a Hedron Crab with Fatal Push against a mill deck. Two Hedron Crabs double the mill rate (6 cards per land drop vs 3). The reasoning about waiting to destroy an Urza's Saga construct is confused - there's no opposing Urza's Saga. Hedron Crab IS the primary threat engine in the mill matchup and should be removed ASAP.

The player intended to equip Shadowspear to Nethergoyf (costing {2} for the equip ability), but instead activated Shadowspear's {1} activated ability ('Permanents your opponents control lose hexproof and indestructible until end of turn'), which does nothing useful here since the opponent has no hexproof or indestructible permanents. This wastes 1 mana and fails to equip the Shadowspear. The player's reasoning explicitly states they want to equip, but they selected the wrong ability.

GPT4om Analyst is a mill deck that needs to discard to hand size. Surgical Extraction can be cast for 2 life (Phyrexian mana) at instant speed and doesn't require mana, making it always castable. However, discarding it isn't terrible since the opponent's graveyard has 5 cards and Surgical Extraction's value is situational. The bigger issue is that Glimpse the Unthinkable requires UB mana and the player only has 1 Island and no black sources on board, making it harder to cast than the other options. Drown in the Loch is the most valuable card to keep as interaction. Archive Trap is free if opponent searches. Fractured Sanity is powerful mill. Surgical Extraction costs 0 mana effectively and could strip key cards like Kozilek's Command or Thought-Knot Seer from the opponent's deck. Discarding Glimpse the Unthinkable (which requires a black source they don't have yet) would have been more reasonable, or one of the redundant Archive Traps since they have 3 copies.

Playing a second Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth is illegal or wasteful due to the legendary rule — there's already one on the battlefield. The player will have to sacrifice one of them immediately, effectively wasting their land drop for the turn. Ifnir Deadlands would have been a strictly better land drop, providing colorless or black mana (with Urborg already in play making it a Swamp too) plus a useful activated ability against opposing creatures.

message: Select an Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth to keep (Legendary Rule)?
annotation_description: Failed to play Ifnir Deadlands from hand during postcombat main. This land produces colorless mana, which is critical for casting Thought-Knot Seer next turn (needing {3}{C}). Missing this land drop delays TKS by at least one turn, losing tempo against a mill opponent where time is critical.

Used Drown in the Loch proactively at sorcery speed to destroy Nethergoyf (a 4/5) rather than advancing the mill game plan with Glimpse the Unthinkable. Drown in the Loch is one of their few interactive/reactive spells that can counter spells at instant speed, and spending it proactively wastes that flexibility. Additionally, the opponent can escape Nethergoyf from graveyard later. Meanwhile, Glimpse mills 10 cards which advances the primary win condition and also powers up future Drown in the Lochs and enables Visions of Beyond's draw-3 mode sooner.

Gem25P Vorthos is resolving their own Pithing Needle's enter-the-battlefield trigger and must name a card. They named Urza's Saga, which is their OWN card currently on their battlefield. Pithing Needle shuts down activated abilities of the named card, so by naming Urza's Saga they are locking out their own Saga's activated abilities (the {T}: Add {C} and the {2}, {T}: Create Construct token abilities). The opponent's board has only Island and Field of Ruin — Field of Ruin has an activated ability that could be problematic (it can destroy nonbasic lands like Urza's Saga), but it requires the opponent to pay mana they may not have. Meanwhile, the opponent has Hedron Crabs in the graveyard and a mill strategy. Naming Shadowspear would also be bad since it's their own card. Given the limited choices of Shadowspear and Urza's Saga, the player should have named Shadowspear (less impactful to lock out) since Urza's Saga is actively providing value through its chapter abilities and construct token creation. However, looking more carefully at the choices presented — they could only choose between Shadowspear and Urza's Saga — both are their own permanents being offered as naming options. This appears to be an interface limitation. Naming Urza's Saga locks out their Saga's mana and construct abilities, which is a significant self-inflicted wound. Naming Shadowspear would only lock out the equip ability and the hexproof/indestructible removal ability, which is much less costly since the Shadowspear is already equipped or can remain as a static buff.

Mishra's Bauble is sitting on the battlefield unused. It costs 0 mana to activate (tap + sacrifice) and provides a free card draw next upkeep plus information about the opponent's top card. There's no reason to hold it - it's pure upside with no downside.

Failed to activate Mishra's Bauble, which is a free ability that draws a card at next upkeep and provides information about the opponent's library top card. There's no reason to hold Mishra's Bauble since it costs nothing to activate and provides pure upside. Sacrificing it also enables Revolt for the three Fatal Pushes in hand and adds another card type to the graveyard for potential Nethergoyf escape.

GPT4om Analyst used Surgical Extraction (paying 2 life, going to 9) to target Divest - a 1-mana sorcery hand disruption spell that is largely irrelevant at this stage of the game. The opponent has already used their discard spells and has a developed board with Thought-Knot Seer. Meanwhile, there are far more impactful targets available: Nethergoyf (which can escape from the graveyard and is a recurring threat), Emperor of Bones (two copies in graveyard, a recursive threat engine), or Urza's Saga (two copies in graveyard, and removing future copies from the opponent's library eliminates a powerful card advantage/tutor engine). Targeting Divest accomplishes almost nothing meaningful while spending 2 life that matters at 11 life against a 19-life opponent with a Thought-Knot Seer on board.

Failed to play a land before combat when holding Swamp and Urza's Saga. Playing Swamp precombat would give 5 mana available for post-combat plays or responses, which is relevant with Kozilek's Command and Orcish Bowmasters in hand. There's no strategic reason to delay the land drop.

Paying 2 life for Surgical Extraction at 4 life drops them to 2, making them vulnerable to Orcish Bowmasters pings and cutting off potential survival lines. While Thought-Knot Seer threatens lethal next turn regardless, going to 2 life means even a Bowmasters trigger from any incidental draw kills them, eliminating any slim chance of stabilizing.

At 4 life (going to 2 from Phyrexian mana), GPT4om targeted their own Hedron Crab with Surgical Extraction instead of the opponent's Nethergoyf. Nethergoyf has escape and two copies are in the opponent's graveyard - these are recurring lethal threats. Removing Hedron Crabs from their own deck/hand provides minimal value since they already have Ruin Crab in hand, while leaving Nethergoyf available to escape back is extremely dangerous at 2 life.

message: Select card named Hedron Crab in the graveyard of GPT4om Analyst (selected 0 of 2)
annotation_description: Surgical Extraction targeting Hedron Crab only allows exiling cards named 'Hedron Crab' from the hand. There are no Hedron Crabs in GPT4om Analyst's hand, so no cards should have been selected. Instead, they selected Glimpse the Unthinkable, unnecessarily giving up a key mill spell.
